title: A factor 1.10 weight range invalidates exact-size moment lists in 834 selected mouse connection models
abstract: We tested whether sparse joint-failure moment lists remain sufficient under bounded efficacy error. We used 1512 Allen V1 Deep Dive and 1438 MICrONS connections with three through eight contacts. At exact cleft-size weights, each list includes all single and pair moments and every nonzero higher-order event term. With each efficacy in its size divided by 1.10 through its size multiplied by 1.10, allowed box corners need omitted moments in 360 and 474 connections. Positive integer probability witnesses prove insufficiency. The event remains fixed in the full box in 788 and 691 cases; 364 and 273 remain unresolved. Necessary corner-support term totals rise from 4505 to 6668 and from 6932 to 11980. Interior sufficiency is not claimed. One animal per map, partial arbors, assumed error bounds, exact moments and absent matched release data limit biological use. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and external regeneration steps support reproduction. External records are excluded.

display.caption: Exact insufficiency witnesses, full-box event stability, and unresolved cases under separate efficacy bounds. Shares describe selected connections, not uncertainty across animals.

citations.reason: Tests the weight stability question left open by its exact moment lists. Extractor reused.
Adopts its efficacy-box model and checks its stable-event counts, with a new moment-sufficiency endpoint.
